Definition: perhaps akin to G2094; "yet," still (of time or degree):--after that, also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any) longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet.
BiblicalUsage: Éti means yet — still, more, after that, the word that keeps a sentence going. He was yet in Galilee, the angel says; the Corinthians are yet carnal, Paul says; and Hebrews says there is yet need of another priest. It is the word for what is still true, and still to come.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe éti is a word of patience: God is not finished, and neither am I. I hold that 'yet' is the space where grace works — what is not yet true can still become true.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
